name: What happens if you don’t compact the backfill after pool removal?

mainEntity.name: What happens if the backfill is not compacted correctly after in-ground pool removal?
mainEntity.text: What happens if the backfill is not compacted correctly after in-ground pool removal?

acceptedAnswer.text: Compaction is what turns a hole in the ground into a stable yard. If the backfill is placed loosely, the soil can settle later and create depressions, cracks in patios, uneven lawns, or drainage problems. The issue can show up months after the removal, which is why some homeowners are surprised by the damage. The risk is higher when the project is a partial fill-in or when the area will later carry hardscape or structures. Homeowners should ask how compaction is performed, whether it is done in layers, and whether any testing or verification is included. For Los Angeles properties, where many owners plan future upgrades after removal, solid compaction is not optional. It is the difference between a clean finish and a long-term problem.
acceptedAnswer.description: If backfill is not compacted correctly, the ground can settle unevenly, sink, crack hardscape, damage drainage, and create soft spots in the yard. The risk is higher over buried shell sections or when loose fill is used. Proper compaction is one of the most important parts of the job.
